Date : 02 February 2026
 Order :
.
Heard learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner.

2. The petitioner wants to raise a so called issue of public interest in respect of licence to the companies which are manufacturing the raw material for production of food items, in which Caramel chemical is used having 4-methyl imidazole, which is harmful to the body and may lead to diseases like cancer.
It is stated that FSSAI permitted the prescribed limit for using 4-methyl imidazole in food product and that limit is 300-200 Mg./Ltd.
However, a company by name Anipra Chemical Private Limted is using the said chemical in producing chemical with 1722 Mg./Ltd.
The 5-pil-88-2017.odt said Caramel is used in other food products, which are also consumed by children.
The products, whose names have been disclosed in the petition, are Bournvita, Boost, Horlicks and all bakery products.

The petitioner, therefore, prays for search to be undertaken under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and stop the production of Caramel chemical Pandharinath Shankarrao Sable vs The Chief Secretary Mantralaya Mumbai ... on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176003681/
1 which is of excess limit and also take cognizance on the complaints/representations made by him.

sentences.text:
3. Heard learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the documents on record.
4.
From the documents, which have been produced on record, we cannot come to the conclusion that the product that is manufactured by M/s. Anipra Chemical Private Limited is used in food products.
There is nothing on record to show as to what are the ingredients those are used while manufacturing Boost, Bournvita, etc.
Unless it is shown that those companies are purchasing Caramel from Anipra Company, we cannot come to the conclusion that such hazardous chemical is being used further in food items.
The petition is vague, not supported by any research.
Rather, it can be said to be a tainted and might have been filed for publicity interest, not public interest.
The first order for leave to amend has been taken on 13.09.2017 and thereafter, the matter was 5-pil-88-2017.odt never taken for circulation also at any point of time.
From 2017 till today, the products like Bornvita, Boost might have been sold in the open market in bulk.
If the petitioner was really interested in safeguarding the health of public, he would not have kept quiet since 2017.
We do not find that there is any point raised so that cognizance can be taken by this Court on the basis of the averments in the petition.
5. The Public Interest Litigation stands dismissed.

[ HITEN S. VENEGAVKAR ] [ SMT. VIBHA KANKANWADI ]
